title: Raspberry Macarons with Raspberry Buttercream
summary: Pink almond macaron shells flavoured with freeze-dried raspberries and filled with a fruity raspberry buttercream.
equipment: piping bag with 1 cm plain nozzle

ingredients.item: egg whites (about 3 large), at room temperature
drops pink or red gel food colouring (optional)
ingredients.note: choose one free from carmine (E120) if you avoid it

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Template
steps.text: draw 24 circles of 3.5 cm on each of 2 sheets of baking paper, 3 cm apart, and turn them over onto the trays.

steps.title: Dry mix
steps.text: grind all 20 g freeze-dried raspberries to powder and set 12 g aside for the buttercream. Pulse the icing sugar, ground almonds and 8 g raspberry powder 10 times, then sieve and discard any coarse bits.

steps.title: Meringue
steps.text: whisk the egg whites on medium to soft peaks, then add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk on high until stiff and glossy, 3-4 min; add the colouring in the last 30 s.

steps.title: Macaronage
steps.text: fold the almond mix into the meringue in 2 lots, then press and fold the batter against the side of the bowl until it falls in a thick ribbon that sinks back into itself in about 20 s. Stop as soon as it does; overmixed batter spreads. Folding knocks out some air so the batter flows into smooth, flat rounds.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: holding the bag upright, pipe to fill each circle, then bang each tray firmly on the worktop 4 times and pop any bubbles with a cocktail stick. Leave 30-45 min until the tops feel dry and are not tacky. Heat the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan). A dry skin on top forces the batter to rise from below and form the foot.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake one tray at a time on the middle shelf 15-17 min until risen with a ruffled foot and the shells lift off the paper cleanly. Cool fully on the tray.

steps.title: Buttercream
steps.text: beat the butter until pale, 2 min, then beat in the icing sugar, the 12 g raspberry powder, cream, vanilla and salt until fluffy.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: pair the shells by size, pipe a blob of buttercream on half and sandwich with the rest. Chill in the airtight box for 24 h so the shells soften slightly, and bring to room temperature 20 min before serving.

tips: A common mistake is overmixing the batter, which spreads into flat, thin shells; test the ribbon often.
An oven thermometer helps, as most ovens run hot or cold and macarons need the right heat.
Weigh everything, including the egg whites.
storage: Keep in an airtight box in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze for 1 month. Serve at room temperature.
